evidence: Receiving DO2 online sensor at t=51.8h: ~10.16 mg/L, ~5x the 2 mg/L hard limit
Source-1/2/3 minima ~7.4-8.2 mg/L occur transiently (t≈119-138h) and recover; receiving shows same benign oscillation pattern
Receiving delayed P assays: 0.023 g/L (t=59), 1.24 g/L (t=179), 3.41 g/L (t=239) — product accumulation on track with source trajectories (source P at t=479: 6.4-7.0 g/L)
Recent DO slope ≈ -0.02 mg/L per hour; no evidence of an imminent oxygen deficit
args.rationale: The receiving fermentation shows no evidence of an oxygen-constraint risk or abnormal behavior at the decision time (t=52h). Online DO2 at t=51.8h is ~10.2 mg/L — roughly 5x the 2 mg/L hard limit. The historical trajectory (dip to ~7.5 mg/L near t=118-138h, recovery to ~11.9 mg/L, then a slow decline of only ~0.02-0.03 mg/L/h over the last ~50h) is consistent across all three source batches, indicating this DO oscillation is normal process behavior, not a developing failure. Extrapolating the recent slow decline, DO would remain far above 2 mg/L for many tens of hours. Product assays (delayed 20h) show P rising steadily: 0.023 g/L (t=59), 0.0 g/L (t=119), 1.24 g/L (t=179), 3.41 g/L (t=239), tracking the source-batch product trajectories. Any intervention (feed reduction, air increase, or combined) would sacrifice product mass or unnecessarily perturb a healthy run: reduce_feed would lower carbon uptake and product formation; increase_air/combined offer no benefit since DO is not limiting. Therefore the supported feasible plan that retains maximum product mass is KEEP.
args.uncertainty: Assays lag by 20h, so the true current product concentration and DO state could deviate from what is known; hidden receiving parameters differ from source, so the DO minimum in the next growth phase could be deeper than the historical ~7.5 mg/L dip. However, even a substantial margin exists (DO ~10 mg/L vs a 2 mg/L limit), and the source-calibrated trajectories suggest the next DO excursion remains well above the limit. If DO were to fall below ~4-5 mg/L, an increase_air intervention would become advisable; current evidence does not support that. No physical safety or outcome guarantee is implied by this recommendation.
